description:
The SSB (Star Schema Benchmark) generator emits a 3-digit p_category value
('MFGR#212') instead of the standard 2-digit value ('MFGR#12'). The
standard SSB Q2.1–Q2.3, Q3.3, Q3.4, and Q4.3 predicates filter on the
2-digit form, so those queries return empty result sets at any scale factor.

Surfaced as a deferred item in the DONE file for
`cross-surface-oracle-remediation` (completed). The DONE file notes the bug
is "Tracked in #870" (a GitHub PR reference), but there is no corresponding
open TODO in `_project/TODO/`, and the vacuous cells are handled by allowlisting
them in the SSB gate rather than fixing the root cause.

The empty results are not a platform divergence or query bug — they are a
data-generation defect. Every platform correctly returns zero rows because
the generator never emits rows with a 2-digit p_category code.

anti_patterns.dont: fix p_category for only one platform
anti_patterns.why: the generator produces the data before any platform loads it
the correct fix is in the generator, not in silencing more cells

preserves.behavior: All other SSB query results remain unchanged (Q1.x, Q2.x not affected by p_category, Q3.x excluding 3.3/3.4)
The cross-surface gate continues to pass for non-SSB benchmarks

prior_art.concept: _binaries/ or benchbox/benchmarks/ssb/ — locate the SSB generator
benchbox/benchmarks/ssb/gate*.yaml — the allowlist entries to remove after the fix
cross-surface-oracle-remediation DONE file — deferred this bug; the allowlist approach is the current workaround

verifications.description: Q2.1 returns non-empty results at SF=0.1
verifications.expected: result set contains at least one row

verifications.description: SSB gate passes without vacuous-cell allowlist entries

work_units.notes:
Run the SSB generator at SF=0.1 and inspect the part table:
  SELECT DISTINCT p_category FROM part WHERE p_category LIKE 'MFGR#2%' LIMIT 10
Confirm 'MFGR#212' (or similar 3-digit) appears; confirm 'MFGR#12' does NOT.
Also count how many of Q2.1–Q2.3, Q3.3, Q3.4, Q4.3 return zero rows.
Check whether #870 was merged and whether the fix is already in the generator.
work_units.summary: Re-validate the generator bug still exists and measure scope

work_units.notes:
Locate the SSB data generator (likely a binary in _binaries/ or a Python
module). Find where mfgr/category codes are composed. The standard SSB
schema assigns p_category as MFGR#{1-5}{1-5} (2-digit suffix), not
MFGR#{1-5}{1-9}{1-9} (3-digit).
work_units.summary: Identify the generator code path that emits p_category

work_units.notes:
Prefer fixing the root cause in the generator. If the generator is a
compiled binary with no source available, add a post-load normalisation
that maps the 3-digit form to the 2-digit form at load time. Document
which approach was taken and why.
work_units.summary: Fix the p_category generation or add a post-load normalisation step

work_units.notes:
After the fix, Q2.1–Q2.3, Q3.3, Q3.4, Q4.3 should return non-empty
result sets. Remove the allowlist/known_divergences entries that were
added to the SSB gate to silence the vacuous cells. Re-run the full SSB
gate and confirm it passes without the exemptions.
work_units.summary: Remove the SSB allowlist entries that paper over the empty cells

work_units.notes:
Run the SSB cross-surface gate across at least two platforms (DuckDB +
one cloud platform). Confirm all 13 SSB queries (Q1.1–Q4.3) return
non-empty, consistent results.
work_units.summary: Verify cross-surface oracle still passes after removing vacuous-cell allowlist entries
